question: By 27 November 2026, how many of the two Bundibugyo-specific vaccine candidates (ChAdOx1 BDBV, mRNA-1469) will have been publicly reported as administered to Tumaini trial participants?

calls.reasoning: As of 16 Nov (11 days before cutoff) no source reports ChAdOx1 BDBV or mRNA-1469 given to a Tumaini participant. WHO recommended both on 4 Nov pending national approvals, still pending per Gavi on 10 Nov, with one site open. Prior from past outbreak trials: adding a new candidate arm usually takes weeks to months after recommendation, so a reported dose within about 23 days of it is uncommon. ChAdOx1 is better placed (about 620k doses' worth of bulk substance made; CEPI said 'shortly' on 23 Oct); mRNA-1469 still needs fill-finish and cold chain. Outcomes are correlated through the shared approval and amendment. No human prediction market found (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold checked; only Ebola-pandemic contracts exist). Pmf about 0.80/0.14/0.06.
calls.dossier:
- Tumaini (NCT07842107) launched 23 Oct 2026 in Bunia with Ervebo as the first candidate (CEPI/ITG press release; WHO DON 6 Nov 2026).
- CEPI, 23 Oct 2026: 'Preparations are underway' for the two CEPI-funded BDBV-specific candidates (Moderna; Oxford/Serum Institute of India) 'to enter the trial shortly.'
- WHO, 4 Nov 2026: TAG-CVP recommended adding ChAdOx1 BDBV and mRNA-1469; they 'will enter the trial following national approvals' (WHO DON625, 6 Nov; UN News).
- Gavi VaccinesWork, around 10 Nov 2026: both enter after national approvals; results expected early 2027; Phase 1 trials done in UK/Canada, others planned or recruiting in Uganda.
- Moderna press release, 4 Nov 2026: Phase 2/3 entry 'subject to regulatory approval'; Moderna to supply mRNA-1469; no shipment or first-dose date given.
- Wikipedia outbreak page (accessed 16 Nov): 'As of 6 November, three candidate vaccines have been approved for inclusion' (Ervebo, ChAdOx1-BDBV-GP, mRNA-1469); no administration of the BDBV-specific candidates reported. Note: 'approved for inclusion' likely means the WHO recommendation, not national regulatory approval.
- ebolaintel.com investigational tracker (accessed 16 Nov): no doses of either candidate reported in Tumaini.
- IFPMA timeline (accessed 16 Nov): last entry Day 171 (4 Nov) is the recommendation; no later entries on approval, shipment or dosing.
- Supply (per question background / TAG-CVP report): about 620k doses' worth of ChAdOx1 bulk substance made at SII; about 12k mRNA-1469 vials made and still needing fill; 1M mRNA doses expected Q2 2027. As of 11 Nov: one open site, 11 rings, more than 80 participants.
- Both directions: ChAdOx1 Phase 1a (UK, 24 Jul) and 1b (6 Oct) exist and the platform is designed for fast arm additions, which supports a quick start; pending DRC regulatory/ethics approval, the protocol amendment, import, site training and blinding logistics point to delay. mRNA also needs an ultra-cold or frozen chain in Ituri.
- Status quo: zero BDBV-specific doses reported in Tumaini as of 16 Nov 2026.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off public reports (WHO, sponsors/developers, CEPI, DRC MoH; secondarily the ebolaintel tracker) explicitly linking a dose to Tumaini; doses in Phase 1 studies (Uganda, UK, Canada) or other DRC trials do not count.
- Event window: any report published on or before 27 Nov 2026 23:59 UTC. Counting from the 4 Nov recommendation, about 52% of the 4 Nov -> 27 Nov span has elapsed as of 16 Nov 2026 13:50 UTC; 11 days remain.
- Reference points: in past outbreaks (DRC 2018-19 adding a second vaccine; Uganda 2022 Sudan-virus candidates arriving about 2 months after declaration and missing the outbreak) the gap from recommendation to first trial dose was usually weeks to months.
- Searched but not found: any DRC national approval (ACOREP/ethics) announcement, protocol amendment notice, dose shipment to DRC, or planned first-dose date for either candidate; no prediction market on this event.
calls.reference_class: Time from WHO recommendation to first dose of a new investigational Ebola-family vaccine candidate in an outbreak trial (DRC 2018-19 J&J addition; Uganda 2022 Sudan-virus candidates; Uganda 2025 ring trial)

calls.reasoning: As of 12-14 Nov the tracker, Gavi and K24 all say both Bundibugyo-specific candidates still await DRC national approval, and no dosing date has been announced. WHO recommended them on 4 Nov, so only about 11 days remain for the protocol amendment, ACOREP/ethics clearance, import, site readiness and a public report that a dose was given. By comparison, Ervebo went from trial authorization (31 Jul) to its first Tumaini dose (23 Oct) in about 12 weeks. ChAdOx1 is plausible as a fast follower because about 620k doses exist; mRNA-1469 has fill-finish and cold-chain constraints. Both are unlikely by 27 Nov. No human prediction market was found.
calls.dossier:
- ebolaintel.com investigational tracker (updated 12 Nov 2026): neither ChAdOx1 BDBV nor mRNA-1469 has been administered in Tumaini; each 'enters the trial once national approvals are in place'.
- WHO news release 4 Nov 2026: expert groups (TAG-CVP) recommend adding both candidates to Tumaini 'following national approvals'; vaccine results expected early 2027.
- Moderna press release 4 Nov 2026: mRNA-1469 advancing to Phase 2/3 in Tumaini 'subject to regulatory approval'; CEPI up to $58.5M for clinical-trial dose manufacturing; no dosing date given; Phase 1 in Canada completed.
- Gavi VaccinesWork 10 Nov 2026: both candidates still await national approvals.
- K24 Digital 14 Nov 2026: candidates 'will enter the trial only after receiving the necessary national approvals'; four rings established, more in preparation (WHO on 11 Nov said >80 participants, 11 rings, 1 site).
- Supply: Serum Institute has manufactured about 620k ChAdOx1 BDBV doses and supplied 3,000 for a Uganda trial (Oxford/BioWorld/Digital Journal reporting); mRNA-1469 has about 12k vials needing fill, with 1M doses expected only by Q2 2027 (TAG-CVP report per question background).
- Tumaini already holds ACOREP (DRC regulator) approval for the base protocol with Ervebo; the platform design is intended to add arms by amendment.
- Timeline analog: Ervebo Phase 3 trial authorized 31 Jul 2026, first Tumaini dose 23 Oct 2026 (about 12 weeks). Sudan-virus ring trial in Uganda in 2025 launched within about 4 days of declaration using a pre-positioned protocol; in 2022, doses arrived about 79 days after declaration.
- Status quo: zero candidates dosed in Tumaini as of 14-16 Nov 2026, and no DRC approval announcement found.
- Resolution: resolves off WHO, sponsor/developer or DRC MoH statements (ebolaintel tracker secondary) that explicitly link a dose to Tumaini/NCT07842107; doses in PARTNERS, EBO-PEP or Phase 1 trials do not count.
- Event window: from now until 27 Nov 2026 23:59 UTC for a published report; about 23 days from the 4 Nov recommendation, of which about 12 days (about 52%) had elapsed as of 16 Nov.
- Searched but not found: any DRC approval or protocol amendment announcement for either candidate; any shipment of candidate doses to DRC; any prediction market on this question (only WHO-pandemic Ebola markets exist).
calls.reference_class: Time from WHO recommendation or authorization of an investigational vaccine to the first trial dose in DRC/East African Ebola outbreak trials (Ervebo-Tumaini 2026 about 12 weeks; Sudan-virus ring trials in Uganda in 2022, weeks to months, and in 2025, days, using a pre-positioned protocol)

calls.reasoning: As of the 12 Nov ebolaintel update, neither ChAdOx1 BDBV nor mRNA-1469 had been dosed in Tumaini. WHO's 4 Nov recommendation is conditional on DRC national approval, which still requires an ACOREP sign-off on a protocol amendment. Searches up to 16 Nov found no approval, shipment or start date. Only 11 days remain, and the Ervebo arm took about 12 weeks from WHO trial authorisation to first dose. Pushing upward: the platform design, extreme urgency, SII already holding about 4,000 clinical doses of ChAdOx1, and sponsors (CEPI/Oxford/MSF) who would announce a first dose quickly. mRNA-1469 has more hurdles (vials still unfilled, cold chain). Approvals are correlated across the two. PMF about 0.65/0.25/0.10. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.

calls.reasoning: As of 12-16 Nov no source reports either BDBV-specific candidate dosed in Tumaini; both still need DRC national/ACOREP approval of a protocol amendment, with one site open. Only ~11 days remain for approval, import, site readiness, dosing and public report; the Ervebo arm took ~12 weeks from authorisation to first dose. ChAdOx1 BDBV has doses on hand and CEPI said 'shortly', making it a plausible fast follower (~21%); mRNA-1469 faces fill-finish and frozen-chain hurdles (~8%), strongly correlated with ChAdOx1 via the shared approval. No human prediction market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers agree on the facts: no BDBV-specific dose reported in Tumaini as of 12-16 Nov; national approval still pending per Gavi (10 Nov) and K24 (14 Nov); no shipment or start date found; ChAdOx1 supply ample, mRNA-1469 constrained. Run 3's mention of 'protocol amendments approved by ACOREP' is ambiguous and is contradicted by every later source saying approvals are pending, so I treated approval as not yet granted, with residual uncertainty. The remaining disagreement is pure judgment about fast-follower speed. I land near Run 1 (PMF ~0.77/0.16/0.07): urgency and a platform design built for fast arm additions are weighed against the ~11-day window, which also has to cover public reporting, and the 12-week Ervebo precedent. I agree with Run 1's reference class and keep it.
